title: English: Reported Speech: Questions
source: Written for Henry (Nov 25): 30 questions on reported (indirect) questions: yes/no with if/whether, wh- questions, word order, backshift, pronouns and time words. American English. Every question has a tier (easy to impossible).

questions.q: "Why are you late?" -> He asked me why I ___ late.
questions.why: Present becomes past.

questions.q: Change to reported speech: Tom asked Mia, "Are you hungry?"
questions.answer: Tom asked Mia if (whether) she was hungry.

questions.q: "Where do you live?" she asked me. Which is correct?
choices: She asked me where I lived.
She asked me where did I live.
She asked me where do I live.
She asked me that where I lived.
questions.why: A reported question has statement word order, with no do/did.

questions.q: Change to reported speech: Ann asked Ben, "Where do you live?"
questions.answer: Ann asked Ben where he lived.

questions.q: "Do you like pizza?" he asked. Which is correct?
choices: He asked me if did I like pizza.
He asked me that I liked pizza.
He asked me do I like pizza.
He asked me if I liked pizza.
questions.why: Yes/no questions use if or whether.

questions.q: Change to reported speech: Mom asked me, "Why are you late?"
questions.answer: Mom asked me why I was late.

questions.q: In a reported question, the word order is like a ___.
questions.why: We say "where I lived", not "where did I live".

questions.q: Change to reported speech: Pim asked Nat, "What are you doing?"
questions.answer: Pim asked Nat what he was doing.

questions.q: Which word can start a reported yes/no question?
questions.why: Use if or whether.

questions.q: Change to reported speech: The teacher asked us, "Did you finish your homework?"
questions.answer: The teacher asked us if (whether) we had finished our homework.

questions.q: He ___ me if I was ready.
questions.why: We ask a question; we do not "say" or "tell" it with if.

questions.q: Change to reported speech: Dan asked Joy, "Can you help me?"
questions.answer: Dan asked Joy if (whether) she could help him.

questions.q: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
choices: He asked me where I was going?
He asked me, where was I going.
He asked me where was I going?
He asked me where I was going.
questions.why: A reported question ends with a period, not a question mark.

questions.q: Change to reported speech: Lek asked me, "Have you seen my phone?"
questions.answer: Lek asked me if (whether) I had seen his phone.

questions.q: "Can you swim?" he asked. -> He asked me ___.
questions.why: can becomes could, and the order is subject + verb.

questions.q: Change to reported speech: Ben asked Fon, "How long have you lived here?"
questions.answer: Ben asked Fon how long she had lived there.

questions.q: "What time does the movie start?" -> She wanted to know what time ___.
questions.why: Backshift and no do/does.

questions.q: Change to reported speech: She asked him, "Will you come to the party tomorrow?"
questions.answer: She asked him if (whether) he would go to the party the next day.

questions.q: "Have you finished?" -> He asked if I ___ finished.
questions.why: Present perfect becomes past perfect.

questions.q: Change to reported speech: The police officer asked the man, "Where were you at 9 p.m. last night?"
questions.answer: The police officer asked the man where he had been at 9 p.m. the night before.

questions.q: "How many brothers do you have?" -> She asked me how many brothers I ___.
questions.why: Present simple becomes past simple.

questions.q: Which two words can start a reported yes/no question?
questions.why: Both mean the same.

questions.q: Which sentence is WRONG?
choices: She asked where did I live.
She asked if I liked it.
She asked what I had eaten.
questions.why: No do/did in a reported question.

questions.q: "Where were you yesterday?" -> He asked where I ___ the day before.
questions.why: Past simple can become past perfect.

questions.q: "Did you see the game last night?" -> Which is the best reported question?
choices: He asked me if did I see the game last night.
He asked me if I will see the game the night before.
He asked me that I had seen the game the night before.
He asked me if I had seen the game the night before.
questions.why: Past perfect, no inversion, and the time changes.

questions.q: "Whose bag is this?" -> He asked whose bag ___.
questions.why: The order stays like a statement; this becomes that.

questions.q: "Who called you?" -> He asked me who ___ me.
questions.why: Who is the subject here, so the order does not change.

questions.q: "Why didn't you call me?" she asked him. -> She asked him why he ___ her.
questions.why: Past simple becomes past perfect.

questions.q: "Do you know when the bus will arrive?" she asked him. -> Which is correct?
choices: She asked him if did he know when would the bus arrive.
She asked him if he knew when would the bus arrive.
She asked him that he knew when the bus would arrive.
She asked him if he knew when the bus would arrive.
questions.why: Two clauses: both keep statement order, and will becomes would.

questions.q: "Are you coming here tomorrow?" she asked me. -> Which has ALL the changes right?
choices: She asked me if I am coming here tomorrow.
She asked me was I coming there the next day.
She asked me if I was coming there the next day.
She asked me if I was coming here the next day.
questions.why: Here becomes there, tomorrow becomes the next day, am becomes was.
